I now have the full picture. Let me lay out what I found before choosing scope.

**Current state — there are two competing patient-login implementations:**

| | `/login` → Patient tab ([Login.tsx:674](src/components/Auth/Login.tsx:674)) | Booking funnel ([PatientLogin.tsx](src/pages/PublicAppointments/auth/PatientLogin.tsx)) |
|---|---|---|
| Reachable at | `/login` | `/facility/:id/appointments/:staffId/otp/:page` |
| Resend countdown | ✅ `careConfig.resendOtpTimeout` | ❌ always-live link |
| Inline OTP errors | ✅ | ❌ global toast only |
| Lands on | `/patient/home` | `book-appointment` |
| Notes | the good one | `navigate()` during render ([:72](src/pages/PublicAppointments/auth/PatientLogin.tsx:72)) |

**Hard blockers for a literal implementation:**
- Design says **6-digit OTP**; backend is `OTP_LENGTH = 5` (`config/settings/base.py:507`). Shipping 6 breaks login.
- Screens 03/05 need a **relationship label** ("Self"/"Father"/"Daughter") and **ABHA ID** per patient — `PublicPatientRead` has neither.
- E1's "2 attempts left / locked 30 minutes", "OTP as a call instead", and the ABHA consent field have no backend contract.
- Flows 3–6 (booking wizard tokens, OP wait times, visit summaries) need API surface that doesn't exist.
- The repo has **none** of the design's semantic tokens (`--soft-background`, `--muted-foreground`, `--strong-border`…) and Badge variants differ — everything needs re-expressing in the repo's `gray-*`/`primary-*` idiom.

The design doc is titled "Patient Login Experience" but contains 18 screens spanning login, home, a 5-step booking wizard, records, reports and visits. Since flows 3–6 are mostly blocked on missing APIs, the scope fork changes the work substantially:

---
name: project-otp-portal-api-gaps
description: Patient (OTP) portal list endpoints omit encounter, so records cannot be scoped per-patient client-side; observation reference_range returns labelled bands with string bounds
metadata:
  type: project
---

Two non-obvious shapes in the patient (OTP) portal API, found while building the
patient login experience on 2026-07-30:

**1. List endpoints carry no patient reference.**
`/api/v1/otp/medication_prescription/` returns only
`{created_date, id, modified_date, name, note, prescribed_by, status, tags}` and
`/api/v1/otp/diagnostic_report/` only
`{category, code, conclusion, created_date, id, modified_date, note, service_request, status}`.
`encounter` is **null/absent on lists** and only populated on the `/{id}/` detail
endpoints (where `encounter.patient` reveals the owner). So prescriptions and
reports **cannot be scoped to the active patient client-side** — filtering on
`encounter.patient.id` silently hides every record. Appointments
(`/api/v1/otp/slots/get_appointments/`) *do* carry `patient`, so those can be
scoped. Proper per-patient scoping needs a backend patient filter on the list
endpoints.

**2. `reference_range` is a set of labelled bands, with string bounds.**
Example: `[{max:"70", interpretation:{display:"Low"}}, {max:"99", min:"70",
interpretation:{display:"Normal"}}, {min:"100", interpretation:{display:"High"}}]`
plus `interpretation: {display:"High"}` on the observation. Two traps: the bounds
are **strings** although `ObservationReferenceRange` declares `min?: number;
max?: number`; and "value falls inside some band" does **not** mean normal —
every band including the abnormal ones matches something. Decide normal/abnormal
from `interpretation.display` (or the matching band's), and when quoting a
reference to a patient pick the band labelled *Normal*, not `reference_range[0]`
(which is the Low band).

**Why:** both caused real bugs — every record hidden, and an out-of-range glucose
(424 against 70-99) displayed as normal next to a misleading "< 70" reference.

**How to apply:** see `src/hooks/usePatientPortalData.ts` and
`src/pages/Patient/records/reportUtils.ts`. Re-check the list payloads before
adding any per-patient filtering; coerce range bounds with `Number()`.

---
name: project-dev-server-emfile
description: npm run dev dies on this machine with EMFILE too many open files; use a production build served by vite preview for browser verification
metadata:
  type: project
---

On this machine `npm run dev` (Vite 8) reliably crashes after a minute or two with:

```
Error: EMFILE: too many open files, watch
    at FSWatcher._handle.onchange (node:internal/fs/watchers)
```

Raising `ulimit -n` does not help (the soft limit is already ~1M); it is the
file-watcher layer, not the shell limit. The crash presents in the browser as
`TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: .../SomeRouter.tsx`
and a "Care has encountered an unexpected error" page — which looks exactly like
a compile error in the named module but is not.

**Why:** this wasted several debugging cycles chasing a phantom code error.

**How to apply:** for browser verification, skip the dev server — build and serve
the static output, which does no watching:

```bash
npm run build && npx vite preview --port 4000 --strictPort
```

Serving on port 4000 matters: `.env.local`'s `REACT_CARE_URL_MAP` keys the API
target off `http://localhost:4000`. After redeploying a build, clear the PWA
service worker and caches in the page or stale assets are served.

Done. Here's where it landed.

## Evaluation of the current code

The design's premise held up: patient login was in poor shape. There were **two competing implementations** — `/login`'s Patient tab (decent: countdown, inline errors) and a worse duplicate in the booking funnel (no countdown, toast-only errors, `navigate()` during render). Neither had a patient-picker step; `PatientUserProvider` just auto-selected `results[0]` with no persistence.

Three constraints shaped what I built:
- **OTP is 5 digits, not 6.** Backend `OTP_LENGTH = 5` (`config/settings/base.py:507`). I drove it from `careConfig.otpLength` (`REACT_OTP_LENGTH`) instead of hardcoding, so flipping to 6 is a one-line change once the backend moves.
- **No relationship or ABHA fields** on `PublicPatientRead`, so the "Self / Father / Daughter" badges and ABHA lines are omitted rather than faked.
- Screens 06/08 (facility & doctor lists) stayed as the existing shared pages — their designed content (wait time, distance, OP hours, on-leave) has no API behind it, and those pages also serve logged-out browsing.

## What shipped

17 files changed, 14 new. All 6 flows: login (01/02/E1), profile picker (03), app shell + switcher sheet (04/05/E3/E4), records + prescriptions (12/13/14), reports (15/16), visits (17/18), booking wizard (09/10/11). `tsc` clean; eslint 0 errors with **zero warnings in every new file** (project total 422 → 416).

## Three real bugs found by verifying against your backend

1. **Records were invisible.** I'd scoped prescriptions/reports by `encounter.patient.id` — but the OTP **list** endpoints omit `encounter` entirely (only `/{id}/` detail has it). That filter hid every record. Removed, with a comment on what a backend fix would need.
2. **An out-of-range result displayed as normal.** `reference_range` is a set of *labelled bands* (Low/Normal/High) with **string** bounds — not a list of acceptable ranges — so "falls inside some band" always matched. A fasting glucose of **424** against `70–99` showed as Normal, next to a reference of `< 70` (the *Low* band). Now flagged amber with "High" and the Normal band quoted.
3. **Page scrolled sideways.** One long LOINC title forced the column to its 480px max on a 375px viewport (missing `min-w-0` in the flex chain).

Also fixed en route: `Success.tsx` read the practitioner from `localStorage` instead of the appointment, and the portal queries now fail silently so deployments lacking those endpoints don't toast "Not Found" at patients.

Two notes for you: `npm run dev` dies on this machine with `EMFILE: too many open files` (a watcher limit, not code) — I verified via `npm run build` + `vite preview`, still running on :4000. And I stopped short of pressing "Confirm appointment", since that would create real data on your backend.

I did **not** commit anything. Want me to open a PR, or split this — login + switcher first, records/reports/visits second?

## Profile is built (screen 19)

**The crash:** the tab bar linked `/patient/profile`, but no route matched it — so it fell through to `/patient/:id` with `id="profile"`, rendering `PatientProfile`, a **staff** component backed by authenticated facility APIs. Worth knowing: that route was already broken for real patient ids too — `/patient/<real-uuid>` rendered "Couldn't Load the Page" under an OTP session. I removed both `/patient/:id` routes from `PatientRouter` (the staff app serves them through `AppRouter`/`PatientRoutes.tsx`, unaffected), which also removes the wildcard that swallowed `/patient/profile`.

**What's on the screen** — [PatientProfileSettings.tsx](src/pages/Patient/PatientProfileSettings.tsx):

- Account card showing the mobile number as the account identity, with the design's framing ("This account belongs to this mobile number")
- "Patients on this number · N", each row tappable to make that profile active — `Active` badge on the current one, `Switch` on the others. Verified: tapping flips the badge, persists to `localStorage`, and updates the header chip.
- "Add a family member" → the standalone registration flow
- Language, wired to the existing `LanguageSelector` (functional, not decorative)
- Sign out via `signOut()`, plus `customDescription` as the deployment footer

**Omitted, because nothing backs them:**

| Design element | Why |
|---|---|
| Owner name + "Edit" | No account-owner record and no edit endpoint — the account *is* the number |
| `UHID KNR/2019/10482` | `PublicPatientRead` has no identifier field |
| `· Self` / `· Father` / `· Daughter` | No relationship field (same gap as screens 03/05) |
| Notifications (SMS + app) | No notification-preference API |
| Consent & data sharing | No consent API |
| `care. v3.2` | Only a build UUID is exposed at runtime, not a release version |
| "Manage" per patient | Its only plausible target (`/patient/:id`) is the broken staff page |

**Two things I changed beyond styling**, because the old page's behaviour didn't fit a booking step:

1. **Dropped the "select a location first" gate.** The old page rendered nothing until you picked an organization from a filter — a dead end as step 1. It now defaults to the patient's **district**, derived by walking up `geo_organization.parent` to `level_cache === 1`. That's the honest basis for the design's "NEAREST TO YOU" heading, so the label reads "Facilities in {district}" (falling back to "All facilities" — which is what your fixture data shows, since those patients have no district parent).

2. **Left the public page alone.** `FacilitiesPage` is also `/facilities` in `PublicRouter` for logged-out browsing, complete with the care logo and `LoginHeader`. Putting wizard chrome on it would have broken that, so `PublicRouter` keeps the old page and only the patient route gets the new one.

**Omitted** — nothing backs them: wait time, departments count, OP hours, and the OP open / Closes 1 PM / No booking badges. Distance ("2.4 km") is the one that's *reachable* — facilities carry `latitude`/`longitude`, so it needs browser geolocation plus a permission prompt. content.text:
All four done, `tsc` and lint clean, no missing i18n keys.

## 1. Organization filter on facility search

Reused `OrganizationFilter` — the same component the old page had. It defaults to the patient's **district** (derived from `geo_organization`), so a state-level deployment doesn't dump every facility on you, and the filter lets you widen or move area. Selection lives in query params so it survives back-navigation.

While wiring it I hit two things worth knowing:
- **`OrganizationFilter` silently ignores its `className` prop** — it's declared in the interface but never applied to the root element. So its layout can't be tuned from outside, and it sits a bit loosely in a 480px column. I removed the className I'd passed rather than leave code implying it works, and I'm flagging it as a separate fix since other pages depend on that component.
- I'd carried `FeatureBadge` chips over from the old card, and on a well-equipped hospital that rendered **eleven badges** and blew the card up. The design has no chips there, so I dropped them — the card is now the clean two-line form.

## 2. Flow stays inside the wizard

New [BookPractitioner.tsx](src/pages/PublicAppointments/BookPractitioner.tsx) as **step 2**, using the public `schedulable_users` endpoint. The chain is now entirely in-wizard, verified end to end:

`/nearby_facilities` (1 of 5) → `/patient/book/:facilityId` (2 of 5) → `book-appointment` (3 of 5 slot → 4 of 5 reason) → success

No hand-off to `FacilityDetailsPage` at any point. I left the practitioner card to name-only — the payload has no qualification, and "Next: Mon 3 Aug · 9:00 AM" would need a slots query per doctor.

## 3. OTP "Change" → back to login

I couldn't reproduce a crash on either the dedicated or booking-funnel route in the current build, so I can't tell you what you hit. But your fix is right regardless: the old handler did a *partial* reset that kept the E.164 number, which is exactly the kind of half-state that goes wrong. `changePhoneNumber` is now `restartLogin` and clears everything including the number, so both the link and the back arrow land on a pristine login screen. Relabelled "Back to login". Verified: phone cleared, Send OTP disabled again, no crash.

## 4. Branding

Care logo now in the patient app header (28px, links home) on Home/Visits/Records/Profile, and in the booking wizard header. For the wizard I restructured the header into two rows — `[back] [logo] … [Step N of 5]` above the title — so nothing gets crowded. Detail screens keep the row for back-arrow + title. It reads `careConfig.mainLogo`, so deployment branding is respected rather than hardcoded.

All four addressed. `tsc` clean, lint clean, no missing i18n keys.

## 2. Wrong patient data (the urgent one) — fixed

Your instinct was right that scoping was the issue. The backend commit you pulled **added a working `patient` query param**, which is what I was missing:

| | prescriptions | reports |
|---|---|---|
| no param | 8 | 2 |
| `?patient=<Manyu>` | 6 | 1 |
| `?patient=<Abhimanyu>` | 0 | 1 |

Previously I'd concluded scoping was impossible (list payloads carry no `encounter`) and was returning **every** linked patient's records — that's the wrong data you saw. Now the queries pass `patient=<id>` **and** carry the id in the React Query key, so the cache can't serve one patient's records to another.

Verified live: Records showed `Active · 6` for Manyu, and switching to Abhimanyu flipped it to `Active · 0` with the confirmation banner — matching the API exactly.

## 1 & 3. Nav — one variant, matching your screenshots

Records was the one that diverged: I'd built summary tiles where the design has underline tabs. Both screens now render the **same** `PatientHeaderTabs` component inside the header, so they're identical by construction:

- Records → `Prescriptions | Diagnostic Reports`
- Visits → `Upcoming · 2 | History · 6`

And the logo now appears **only when there's no title** — i.e. Home alone. Verified: Home has the logo, Records/Visits/Profile have titles and no logo.

## "Change" on step 4 → switcher sheet

Swapped the link for the shared `PatientSwitcherSheet` and deleted `PatientSelect.tsx` plus its route. `PatientRegistration`'s booking-flow back-link now returns to the slot step instead of the dead page. Grep confirms no `patient-select` references remain.

**Not visually verified:** there are no bookable slots in your fixture data for any of the next 6 days, so I couldn't reach step 4 through the UI. The change is typechecked and the old route/page are gone, but I haven't seen the sheet open there.

## Registration bugs (from the previous round)

- **Dark unreadable page** — my regression from removing the sidebar shell; now uses the app's 480px column. Fixed and verified.
- **`sm:ml-64`** phantom sidebar offset in the footer — removed.
- **`SYSTEM__govt_org_type__undefined`** rendered as a raw key when an org has no `govt_org_type`; now falls back to "State". Fixed and verified.
- **"Unsaved changes" prompt fired on a *successful* save** — `isCreatingAppointment` is always false outside the booking flow, so the guard reduced to `isDirty`. Now also checks `!hasSaved && !isCreatingPatient`. Fixed, **not verified end-to-end** — a stray click knocked me out of the form before I completed a registration, so no test profile was created.
- Gender/age radios were four full-width rows; now a 2-column grid.

One thing I'd flag rather than fold in: `OrganizationFilter` **ignores its own `className` prop**, and `GovtOrganizationSelector` is deprecated in favour of `GovtOrganizationPicker` (which takes an `Organization` object, not an id string). Both are shared with the staff app, so they want their own change.

content.text:
Fixed and verified.

## The actual cause wasn't where I first looked

I started in `PatientUserProvider` (which sent signed-out users to `/`), but that code never ran. `AuthUserProvider` picks the router by auth state:

- no token → `PublicRouter`
- patient token → `PatientRouter`
- staff token → `AppRouter`

So a signed-out hit on `/patient/home` went to `PublicRouter`, matched nothing, and fell through to `{routeResult || <Login />}` — rendering the **staff** login while leaving `/patient/home` in the address bar. That's the wrong form *and* a lying URL.

## Fix

`PublicRouter`'s fallback is now path-aware — unmatched `/patient/*` paths redirect to the patient login instead of silently rendering the staff form:

```tsx
const isPatientPath =
  !!path && path.startsWith("/patient") && path !== "/patient/login";

{routeResult || (isPatientPath ? <Redirect to="/patient/login" /> : <Login />)}
```

Two related changes while I was in there:

- **`PatientUserProvider`** now sends a session that disappears mid-use to `/patient/login` rather than `/` (the landing page). Defensive, but it's the correct destination for the sign-out-in-another-tab case.
- **Sign out** from the Profile screen landed on the staff `/login`, because the shared `signOut()` hardcodes that. It now awaits `signOut()` then goes to `/patient/login`.

## Verified

| path (signed out) | result |
|---|---|
| `/patient/home` | → `/patient/login`, "Sign in to your health records" |
| `/patient/records` | → `/patient/login` |
| `/login` | unchanged — staff form with Staff/Patient tabs |
| `/` | unchanged — public landing page |

`tsc` clean, lint clean, no missing i18n keys.

One thing I deliberately left out: the redirect drops the intended destination, so signing in from `/patient/records` lands on home rather than back on records. Worth adding a `?redirect=` round-trip if you want it — say the word.

Also worth flagging: your changes are now all **staged** (`git status` shows `A`/`M`, nothing committed). `.env` is staged too — that's your endpoint switch to the local backend, which you probably don't want in the PR.

content.text:
Both fixed, and the whole `src` tree now has **zero eslint errors**.

## The two lint failures

**`GovtOrganizationSelector` deprecated** — swapped for `GovtOrganizationPicker`. It takes an `Organization` object rather than an id string, so the form holds the object in local state and commits `organization.id` to the field. I mirrored the staff form's completeness rule rather than inventing one:

```tsx
required={MIN_GEO_ORG_LEVELS == null}
requiredDepth={MIN_GEO_ORG_LEVELS}
```

with a local `isGeoOrganizationComplete()` that checks the configured depth, or falls back to "must be a leaf" — so a half-finished cascade commits `""` and fails validation instead of submitting a partial location.

**`form.watch()` not memoizable** — replaced with `useWatch({ control, name })` for `ageInputType`, and the same for the age preview, which was calling `form.getValues("age")` three times per render.

Verified on `/patient/add-profile`: renders, no crash, label reads `State*`, no raw `SYSTEM__govt_org_type` key leaking.

A side effect worth noting: the picker supersedes the `SYSTEM__govt_org_type__undefined` fallback I patched into `GovtOrganizationSelector` last round. I've left that patch in — the selector is still used elsewhere and the bug was real there too.

## "Log in as Patient" → new login page

The trigger now navigates to `/patient/login`. First attempt via `onValueChange` didn't fire — Radix won't emit it for a trigger with no matching `TabsContent` — so it's on the trigger's own `onClick`.

That made the inline patient tab dead, so I removed it along with the duplicate OTP implementation I flagged at the very start: `isOtpSent`/`phone`/`otp`/`otpError`/`otpValidationError`/`resendOtpCountdown`, the countdown effect, both OTP mutations, `handlePatientLogin`, `resetPatientLogin`, and the whole `<TabsContent value="patient">` block, plus the now-unused imports.

**`Login.tsx`: 809 → 556 lines.** There is now exactly one patient OTP implementation in the codebase.

Verified: `/login` still shows the staff form with both tabs; clicking "Log in as Patient" lands on `/patient/login` with "Sign in to your health records".

`tsc` clean, 0 eslint errors across `src`, no missing i18n keys. Still nothing committed — and `.env` is still staged with your local endpoint switch, which you'll want to unstage before the PR.
